previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with multiple myeloma, stage V chronic kidney disease on hemodialysis, hemolytic anemia, and type 2 diabetes, was admitted for acute lower extremity weakness. Evaluation revealed a urinary tract infection with elevated lactate and leukocytosis, consistent with sepsis. He was transfused for acute on chronic anemia and treated with a seven-day course of ceftriaxone. MRI spine showed severe cervical stenosis without cord compression, referred to spine clinic, but no myeloma-related spinal cord compression. Weakness improved, attributed to infection, anemia, and deconditioning. His C. difficile taper was extended due to antibiotic exposure. He completed treatment, regained baseline strength, and was discharged home with services, continuing dialysis, chemotherapy follow-up, and a seven-day extended vancomycin course.
